title: DON'T USE NATIONWIDE
text:
I got nationwide pet insurance for my dog a couple years ago. The first year or two I did not have to use it, as we only needed standard wellness check-ups. However this year my pet got sick and needed hospitalization. I currently pay $70/month for a max reimbursement of $7,500. Recently I got a letter in the mail saying that my current policy is going away and my new policy is $326/month with a max reimbursement of $5,000 for illness. So nearly $4k annually to get at most $5k reimbursed for illness. Furthermore since she is still being treated for the illness, if I moved to a new insurance provider this would be considered a pre-existing condition and likely wouldn't be covered.  

So basically even if it seems like a good deal now, it's possible if you need something in the future they will screw you over in the long run. I brought this up to my vet and she said she has heard lots of complaints from people with Nationwide pet insurance, and often hears "Nationwide is NOT on your side."

To be fair, their app is easy to use and submit claims, and I did find the 24/7 vet line to be helpful. But I now wish I would have gone with a different provider to begin with.

The overall concern for me were the unexpected costs that can occur, being a single fur parent I need to make sure cost isn’t the biggest factor. This gives me the most peace of mind!

title: It was quick and easy
text: It was quick and easy!  You told me what I was and wasn't getting for my premium.  Some of the other optional benefits didn't explain what I'd get at all - 'You'll get a payment right away for you to chose how to use it' - is that payment $200 or $2000 - in what instances if I'm suddenly sick or injured would I not get it.  Tell me what I'm paying for - and you did that!
